predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, flat hazard within a problem: Mantel-Haenszel rate ratio of right finishes per 1,000 alive tokens, window [12,000, 16,384) against window [4,000, 8,000), stratified by problem, for the cued base on hard328. The late-degradation rival (solve chance falls within the problem late in the answer) predicts about 0.45, near the unstratified population ratio. This mechanism predicts about 0.85 because the population fall is selection.
predictions.recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0, then the first row in file order for each (problem_index, sample). A row is a cap hit if cap_hit is true, or cap_hit is missing and finish_reason == 'length'. A row is a right finish if score_v3 == 1 and it is not a cap hit; null or missing score_v3 is not right. Let n = n_new. Windows: early [4000, 8000), late [12000, 16384). Alive mass of a row in window [a, b) = max(0, min(n, b) - a) / 1000. Right event of a row in window [a, b) = 1 if the row is a right finish and a <= n < b, else 0. Cap hits contribute mass and never an event. For each problem p, sum over its kept rows: E_p (early events), ME_p (early mass), L_p (late events), ML_p (late mass); M_p = ME_p + ML_p. Skip problems with M_p == 0. Statistic = [sum_p L_p * ME_p / M_p] / [sum_p E_p * ML_p / M_p]. If the denominator is 0, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.note: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (in git; read from the worktree, copied out of git HEAD into runs/theory-tests/ if missing). Every row has attempt, cap_hit (boolean), finish_reason, score_v3 and n_new, so the finish_reason fallback is never used. Implemented as written: Mantel-Haenszel weights ME_p/M_p and ML_p/M_p, problems with M_p == 0 skipped, a zero denominator gives refuted_without_number. The recipe is unambiguous, so alt_measured is the crude pooled (unstratified) late/early rate ratio over the same rows. It is a comparison number, not another reading: the rival puts the stratified MH ratio near the crude ratio. n = problems with M_p > 0. Bootstrap resamples per-problem (E, ME, L, ML) tuples; a resample with a zero denominator scores inf. Caution: problems with no right finish in either window add nothing to the statistic, so the ratio depends on the few problems that have early or late events, and the interval may be wide.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, spread of right-answer lengths within a problem on long problems: the median absolute log ratio of the lengths of two right attempt-0 answers to the same problem, on problems where the base hit the cap in at least one of its 4 samples. A memoryless solve time spreads right finishes across the whole window (about 0.45). A fixed-work-length rival (each problem needs about L tokens of derivation) predicts a narrow spread, about 0.2-0.25.
predictions.recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0, then the first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right finish: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit. Long problems: problem_index values with at least one kept cap-hit row. Among long problems keep those with at least 2 right-finish rows. For every unordered pair (i, j) of right-finish rows of the same problem, compute d = |ln(max(n_new_i, 1) / max(n_new_j, 1))|. Statistic = median of d over all pairs pooled across problems (even count: mean of the two middle values). If fewer than 5 pairs exist, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Same base cue file. Long problems = at least one kept attempt-0 cap hit; of those, keep problems with >= 2 right finishes. d = |ln(max(n_i,1)/max(n_j,1))| over all unordered pairs within a problem, pooled; median takes the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Fewer than 5 pairs gives refuted_without_number. Ambiguity: pooling pairs gives a problem with 3 rights 3 pairs and one with 2 rights 1 pair. Other reading (alt_measured): count each problem once, as the median over problems of each problem's median d. n = number of problems kept. Bootstrap resamples problems (each entry holds its tuple of right-finish lengths). Caution: a problem has at most 4 samples and needs a cap hit, so at most 3 rights and 3 pairs. The pooled set may be small, which makes the median coarse.

predictions.experiment: Cause, the per-token rate sets the cap gain: ratio of Think-SFT's pooled right-finish rate per 1,000 alive tokens in [12,000, 16,384) to the cued base's in the same window, hard328, attempt 0, 4 samples. The mechanism gives the larger 32k gain to Think-SFT because its rate is higher.
predictions.recipe: Files: A = studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (Think-SFT cue) and B = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (base cue). In each file keep rows with attempt == 0 (rows with no attempt field count as attempt 0), then the first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right finish: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit. For each file: R = number of kept right-finish rows with 12000 <= n_new < 16384; M = sum over all kept rows of max(0, min(n_new, 16384) - 12000) / 1000. Rate = R / M. Statistic = Rate_A / Rate_B. If M or R of B is 0, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.note: A = studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl, B = the base cue day1_3 file (both in git). attempt == 0 (a missing attempt counts as 0; every row has one), first row per (problem_index, sample). R counts right finishes with 12000 <= n_new < 16384. M sums max(0, min(n_new,16384)-12000)/1000 over all kept rows, cap hits included. M or R of B equal to 0 gives refuted_without_number. alt_measured is None: I found no real second reading (a cap hit's n_new is at least the cap, so counting cap-hit score_v3 == 1 rows would add no events inside the window). groups line: problems per file. n = min of the two. Bootstrap resamples problem_index with the A and B rows of a problem kept together, and recomputes both pooled rates. Caution: the base's late right count is probably small, around a dozen, so the ratio and its interval are sensitive to a few events.

predictions.experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on problems where the base is right in none of its 4 attempt-0 samples, extra tokens should buy almost nothing because the problem's own rate is near zero. Measured on fresh restarts (attempt >= 1), which under a memoryless process spend tokens at the same per-problem rate a raised cap would: the fraction of restart rows that are right.
predictions.recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Attempt-0 set: rows with attempt == 0, first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit (null or missing score_v3 is not right). Z = problem_index values with at least one attempt-0 cap hit and 0 right attempt-0 rows. Restart rows = all rows with attempt >= 1 and problem_index in Z (every such row counts, file order irrelevant). Statistic = (restart rows that are right) / (restart rows). If there are no restart rows, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Base cue day1_3 file. Z = problems whose kept attempt-0 rows (first per (problem_index, sample)) include at least one cap hit and no right finish. Restart rows = every row with attempt >= 1 in Z. Right = score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit, applied to restart rows as well. No restart rows gives refuted_without_number. Ambiguity: the recipe defines Right next to the attempt-0 set, so it is unclear whether a restart row that hit the cap but has score_v3 == 1 counts. Other reading (alt_measured): count score_v3 == 1 alone. n = problems in Z with at least one restart row (the bootstrap unit). The rows number more. Caution: restarts happen only after a cap hit, so problems with more cap hits contribute more restart rows and pooling weights them more heavily.
